Honestly? I'd have said more. Earlier. To all of you.

I spent a lot of this time managing things and keeping the peace and making sure everybody was okay and I never really just... said what I was actually feeling. I do that at home too. I'm not great at letting people in and out here it wasn't any different. I kept things close to my chest when I probably should've just put them out there.

I'd have talked to you about the bottle the same day it happened instead of letting it sit. Not to embarrass you, just to deal with it before it had a chance to grow into something worse. I let that go too long.

And I'd have spent more time with Michelangelo just sitting and talking and less time worrying about whether he was pulling his weight with the firewood. He needed somebody to just be present with him more than he needed to collect wood. I knew that and I still kept defaulting back to the task list.

I think I'd also have told DaVinci what he meant to the group more. He kept everybody moving when the rest of us were dragging and I don't think I ever actually said that to him out loud.

I think I just... I don't want it to be over. Which is insane, right? We almost died out here. Multiple times. We were cold and hungry and scared and I watched a plane fly away and felt like the floor dropped out from under me. And now rescue is right there and I can't make myself move.

I think it's because out here it was simple. Not easy, but simple. You wake up and you know exactly what matters and exactly what you have to do and there's no room for any of the other stuff. Out here I actually said things. To all of you. Things I don't think I've ever said to anybody back home.
